GDP = the total value of goods and services produced in a country
welfare state = a system in which the state provides healthcare, education and support for those in need
tax evasion = illegally hiding income or profits to avoid paying tax
tax avoidance = using legal loopholes to pay as little tax as possible
income tax = a tax paid on money you earn from work or investments
public spending = money the government spends on services and investment
budget deficit = the amount by which government spending exceeds income
national debt = the total amount a government owes
austerity = government policy of cutting spending to reduce debt
unemployment rate = the percentage of the workforce without a job and seeking one
means-tested benefit = state help given only if your income is below a limit
income inequality = large gaps between what rich and poor people earn
universal basic income = a regular sum paid by the state to every citizen
unemployment benefit = money paid by the state to people who have lost their jobs
means-tested = available only if your income and savings are below a set level
privatisation = selling a state-owned company or service to private owners
nationalisation = bringing a private company or sector under state ownership
austerity measures = government cuts in spending to reduce a budget deficit
state-owned = owned and controlled by the government
subsidy = money given by the state to keep prices down or support an industry
